findings: Caller mitigation: getAllMediaItems result/chunk requestId must equal active request ID. Cancel clears active ID, chunk buffers and watchdog, and aborts detector signal. Reducer-only stale fetch outcome is not direct proof of a normal UI failure.

Residual completion window: runDuplicateDetection awaits logger.finalize after detection then clears active ID and dispatches SCAN_COMPLETE without checking signal or operation identity again. Cancellation/new operation during that await can publish stale completion; static ordering, not browser race reproduction.
Caller mitigation: defaultKeptSets recomputes selectDefaultKeep from remaining group members. A stale originalMediaKey alone does not establish deletion of every remaining member.

Restored override keys are filtered by valid group ID only, not membership. A nonempty kept override containing only absent keys can make handleTrash select every present member. Stored-data reachability not runtime-qualified.

Incremental fetch loads previous mediaItems using account-only validity and newest creation timestamp. Merge retains all cached-only items, with no deletion reconciliation or refilter against changed dateRange in this source. Full scanMode still uses this incremental media fetch.
Saved results load independently of mount health check and are not validated against current state in the storage callback. Unknown-account results may later be relabelled by reducer.
Health results dispatch unconditionally regardless of scanning/trashing state. Trash/restore results do not use active request correlation in this listener. No live messages sent.
Undo restores UI snapshot optimistically before server acknowledgement; restore failure is console-only here. Snapshot lacks account identity.
Chunks deduplicate repeated indices, but count/index bounds and consistent totalChunks are not validated in this source. A 150-second fetch-silence watchdog exists and resets on progress.
limits: Static caller analysis; no React mounting, browser message delivery, account connection or trash/restore executed.
Earlier reducer controls remain scoped to synthetic transitions; caller mitigations recorded explicitly.
